# Direct method seeds with fixed nominal contexts

Owned Java inputs retain one method-owned Object seed beside an independent
String context and boolean values. The fixed result has a closed generic
ancestor and marker interface. Original IOException declarations remain intact.

Frozen callers and a future subclass compare 128 cases twice for source and SDK
declarations. They observe exact receiver, seed, context and result identities,
context snapshots before receiver callbacks, primitive values, callback order
and partial writes, null dereferences, early and late casts, and exact checked,
runtime and Error objects. Thirteen wrong programs qualify the observer. Eight
Signature controls preserve every original Code body and descriptor. Every
recovered source compiles; original metadata and Exceptions are compared.
Only these owned fixtures and harnesses execute.

Source controls compare the exact SDK-decoded method Signature before invoking NeverD. The parameterized fixed context control remains encoded by D8; malformed arguments on a known program result can instead be normalized by D8 and would not test the intended rejection. The earlier normalized-result observation remains private diagnostic evidence.
